item.title: Police avert Obi-Kwankwaso, APC supporters clash in Calabar
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu CALABAR Police and other security operatives on Wednesday prevented a possible violent clash in Calabar, Cross River State, between hundreds of supporters of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso and a large group of All Progressives Congress (APC) supporters on a campaign walk. The meeting, organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, was to feature Obi, its presidential candidate, and Kwankwaso, his running mate. It was scheduled to be held at a hotel along Murtala Mohammed Highway, near the U.J. Esuene Stadium. The APC supporters, who had mobilised in large numbers for a street rally in the same area, included members of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria, ALGON, and other party faithful. Tension rose as both groups met in front of the hotel. Hundreds of Obi and Kwankwaso supporters had gathered there, partially blocking the highway in an apparent attempt to stop the APC supporters from reaching the venue. Security operatives separated the two groups and diverted the APC crowd. The hotel management later restricted access to its premises as security personnel maintained order around the facility. A police officer, who declined to be named, said the intervention was necessary to forestall bloodshed. “What we have done is very necessary; otherwise, it would have been a bloody scene,” he said. Confirming the incident to Vanguard in a WhatsApp message, the Cross River State Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, said the command acted to avert a breakdown of law and order. He stated, “Cross River State Police Command, through timely intervention and constructive engagement, helped avert a possible confrontation between participants at a presidential town hall meeting organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) at Hotel along the Murtala Mohammed Highway in Calabar and a group of supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) undertaking a rally/road walk towards the Governor’s Office. “Upon the convergence of both groups in front of the Metropolitan Hotel, police officers promptly engaged them, appealing to all parties to exercise restraint, maintain peace and ensure that their respective activities were conducted peacefully and in accordance with the law.” Officials of both political camps had not commented on the incident as of the time of filing this report, although some senior APC officials were seen leaving the vicinity of the NDC meeting. Obi and Kwankwaso had not also arrived at the venue as of the time of this report, while party stalwarts and supporters thronged the hotel premises and its frontage. item.title: Slavery reparations ‘not feasible’ for UK – Foreign minister
item.description: Britain’s Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said it was “not feasible” for the country to pay reparations for slavery, after King Charles III expressed remorse amid calls for a formal apology and compensation. “It’s not the right answer. It’s not practical. It’s not feasible for us, but there are things we can work on co-operatively,” Miliband told the BBC in an interview aired Wednesday. He added that London would not “shift our position on reparations”. Miliband also hinted that Britain could issue a long-demanded formal apology for its role in the slave trade next year when it hosts a G20 leaders’ summit. Asked whether the UK could reach that point by the meeting in Manchester next November, Miliband said: “Broadly speaking, yes”. But he insisted an apology would not pave the way for financial compensation. At the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda, Prime Minister Andy Burnham floated a “debt reset” plan for the poorest Commonwealth countries that could alter interest rates on repayments. Burnham told reporters on Tuesday: “I’ve been very clear that we do not support reparations … but it’s not the case that we don’t support countries in the Commonwealth around development helping them with debt issues that they’ve got”. Britain’s pivotal role in slavery has long strained relations with its former colonies. Burnham said he would have “difficult conversations” to safeguard the Commonwealth’s future. In a tense Commonwealth meeting in Samoa in 2024, countries backed talks over reparatory justice after Britain, then under Keir Starmer’s leadership, tried to avoid addressing the issue. Burnham’s change of tack has not gone down well at home, with opposition Conservative party leader Kemi Badenoch and the right-wing press criticising his approach. King Charles went further than previous royals when he expressed his “horror”, but stopped short of apologising and stressed Britain’s role in eventually abolishing slavery. The king opened the summit — part of a nine-day Caribbean tour — calling slavery a “monstrous injustice” that “still casts a shadow over these islands and other members” of the 56-nation group of mostly former British colonies. Charles and Queen Camilla are to end their Caribbean tour and depart from Antigua and Barbuda on Wednesday. item.title: I drove taxi to fund my education in US – Tinubu
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has recalled how he worked as a taxi driver and took up other jobs to finance his education in the United States, saying his personal experience has shaped his commitment to expanding educational opportunities for Nigerian children. Tinubu, in a post on his X handle on Wednesday, said he postponed starting school for several months to save enough money before eventually moving to Chicago, where he worked different jobs to pay his way through university. “When I first arrived in the United States as a young man, I drove a taxi to earn money for my education. I even had to postpone starting school for several months to save enough,” he said. “When I eventually got to Chicago, I worked different jobs to support myself and pay my way through university. I know what it means to worry about tuition, accommodation and how to make ends meet while pursuing an education.” The president said he understood the difficulties of paying tuition and accommodation while pursuing an education, adding that every Nigerian child deserved equal opportunities regardless of their background or their parents’ financial circumstances. He said education remained a major priority of his administration, citing the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, through which he said over N372 billion had been provided in student loans for institutional fees and upkeep. Tinubu also disclosed that the government’s technical and vocational education programme had attracted more than 2.8 million applications, while 38 technical colleges had been rehabilitated. According to him, students in federal and selected state technical colleges now benefit from free school fees, boarding, textbooks and uniforms. On university education, Tinubu said his administration had reached a new agreement with the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, providing for a 40 per cent increase in academic staff remuneration and measures to improve stability in the country’s universities. He added that the government was committed to ensuring that students completed their courses within the stipulated period. “A four-year course must take four years. Our young people deserve to complete their education on time and get on with their lives,” he said. Tinubu further said the Federal Government was investing N110 billion in the rehabilitation of 24 medical schools, while annual nursing enrolment had increased from 28,000 to 115,000. He said enrolment in medical and dental programmes had also risen from 5,000 to 12,000, noting that Nigeria needed to strengthen its capacity to train more healthcare professionals locally. Tinubu added that over one million children who were previously out of school had returned to learning, while his administration was investing in teacher development, expanding educational opportunities for girls and implementing a new national curriculum that restores Nigerian history to classrooms. item.title: Teenager pushed down from two-storey building in Imo dies
item.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka, Owerri Seventeen-year-old Chiamaka Chukwuokore, who was allegedly pushed from a two-storey building by Ifeanyi Chukwu Joseph, has died after medical personnel battled to save her life. Ifeanyi, said to be a boyfriend to Chiamaka’s aunt, had reportedly pushed her down from the building at Mbonu Ojike Street, Ikenegbu Layout, Owerri, on Sunday, following an altercation between him and the victim. The incident led to the arrest of Ifeanyi, who the police said is still in their custody. The spokesman of the police in the state, Henry Okoye, in a statement on Wednesday, confirmed Chiamaka’s death, adding that investigations were still ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. “The Imo State Police Command wishes to inform the public that 17-year-old Chiamaka Chukwuokore, who was allegedly pushed from a two-storey building by Ifeanyi Chukwu Joseph, aged 26, on November 1, 2026, along Mbonu Ejike Street, Ikeneagbu, Owerri, has sadly died. “The victim, who sustained serious injuries from the incident, was rushed to a hospital for medical attention but unfortunately succumbed to her injuries in the evening of November 3, 2026, while receiving treatment. “The suspect remains in police custody as investigations continue to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that justice is served. “The Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, commiserates with the family of the deceased and assures the public that a thorough investigation is ongoing. “The Command urges members of the public to remain calm, avoid spreading unverified information and allow the police to carry out their duties professionally,” the statement read. item.title: 4,000 Newly Employed Public Servants To Strengthen A’Ibom Civil Service, Says Gov Eno
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has said the recruitment of 4,000 new civil servants was aimed at filling identified vacancies and strengthening the state’s public service for improved efficiency and service delivery. Governor Eno spoke on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, during an orientation programme for the newly recruited workers at the Ibom Tropicana Event Centre, Uyo. The orientation follows his earlier announcement directing the newly employed civil servants to resume work on October 1, 2026. Explaining the rationale behind the recruitment, Eno said a staff verification exercise conducted after he assumed office revealed more than 2,000 ghost workers, as well as several employees who had retired but remained on the payroll. He explained that after addressing the identified irregularities, the government found it necessary to fill the resulting vacancies and strengthen the workforce. According to him, the recruitment was not intended to inflate the size of the civil service but to address manpower shortages and improve its capacity to deliver public services. “There was a huge vacancy gap in the Service, so we are not recruiting to bloat the service but to strengthen and make the public service more efficient for excellent work output,” the Governor said. A cross-section of the newly employed civil servants on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. He charged the new employees to demonstrate commitment, discipline, and professionalism in their duties, urging them to bring fresh ideas and innovation into the system. Governor Eno further reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the prompt payment of salaries and gratuities. Earlier, the Head of the Civil Service, Mrs. Elsie Peters, expressed confidence in the quality of the newly recruited workforce, describing the orientation and training as important steps towards revitalising the state civil service. She acknowledged Governor Eno’s support for the public service and expressed optimism that the new employees would contribute to improved performance and greater efficiency across government institutions. Some of the newly recruited civil servants expressed excitement over their appointments, describing the opportunity to join the state workforce as a significant milestone. They also commended the recruitment process, which they described as fair and credible, saying their selection was based on merit and not favouritism. Among the beneficiaries who shared their experiences were Jennifer Ekott, Glory Wilson and Imo Obot, who expressed appreciation for the opportunity to serve the state. The orientation programme is expected to familiarise the new employees with the values, expectations and responsibilities of the public service as they begin their careers in the Akwa Ibom State Civil Service. item.title: Elon Musk jokes about GOP election defeat after spending record sums on party
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk joked on Wednesday about Republicans’ defeat in US midterm elections after spending hundreds of millions of dollars to help the party. Democrats seized control of the US Congress on Tuesday, capturing both the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning rejection of President Donald Trump’s political agenda. “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” Musk said on X, including the shrug emoji. Musk contributed nearly half a billion dollars to Republican political efforts, making him the largest individual contributor in a federal election cycle since unlimited election spending was allowed in 2010, according to campaign finance tracker OpenSecrets. His donations have mostly gone to his Republican-leaning America PAC, as well as to the Republican Senate Leadership Fund super PAC. The SLF used Musk’s $158 million in donations in September to support Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate candidate in Texas. Democrat James Talarico defeated Paxton, a close ally of Trump, to become the first Democrat to win statewide office in Texas since 1994. Talarico took aim at Musk at a victory rally in Austin. “In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths. The richest man in the world, the most powerful man in the world and the entire Washington, DC establishment,” he said. item.title: South Africa votes under shadow of service failures
item.description: South Africans vote Wednesday in a closely watched local government election, with parties battling for control of major cities in a contest expected to offer a measure of the national mood before the next national polls. The vote comes as a weary electorate contends with crumbling infrastructure, dry taps, persistent inequality and unemployment above 30 percent, deepening public disillusionment with the political establishment. Polling stations opened at 7:00 am (0500 GMT) and will close at 9:00 pm (1900 GMT). “I want things to change… people must get work. People mustn’t suffer,” said Thembinkosi Somana, 50, who was first in line to cast his ballot at a polling station in Langa, Cape Town’s oldest township. In Johannesburg, Andrea Smith, 41, who works in human resources, arrived at a polling station with her husband and child, hoping the election would bring change to the country as a whole. “We shouldn’t be having to worrying about electricity and water. It’s been going on for years,” she told AFP. More than 29 million voters are registered but the last municipal elections, in 2021, drew fewer than half of them to the polls, with turnout at just 46 percent. Of the 2.6 million people approved to cast special votes over two days, only 1.4 million did so, the electoral commission said Tuesday. The African National Congress (ANC), which led the country’s liberation struggle, remains projected to emerge as the largest party nationally, but polls point to a further erosion of its support. Once the dominant force in South African politics, the party of anti-apartheid hero Nelson Mandela fell below 50 percent of the vote for the first time in the 2021 municipal elections. It suffered further losses at the 2024 national vote, securing just over 40 percent and forcing it to share power in a government of national unity with nine other parties. The liberal Democratic Alliance (DA), the country’s second-largest party, has set its sights on Johannesburg, campaigning hard to capitalise on service delivery failures in the ANC bastion. Meanwhile, the breakaway opposition uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) party, led by former president Jacob Zuma, is mounting a strong challenge for the east coast port city of Durban. MK made a dramatic electoral breakthrough in 2024, drawing support away from the ANC to finish third nationally, with 14.5 percent of the vote. “We are going to start by taking back our country here,” Zuma said on Sunday in Durban, a city at the centre of growing anti-migrant sentiment that has become a prominent theme of the election campaign. – Hung municipalities – South Africans elect municipal councillors, who then choose mayors and form the administrations that will run their cities. With outright majorities far from assured in several major cities, the vote could usher in another round of complex coalition negotiations, as parties bargain over the alliances needed to govern. item.title: Oyebanji seeks FG’s Support To Boost Livestock Development, Job Creation
item.description: Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, is seeking increased support and collaboration from the Federal Government to strengthen livestock development in the state as part of efforts to create more jobs, generate wealth and expand economic opportunities for the people. The Governor appealed on Tuesday while receiving the Minister of Livestock Development, Mallam Idi Mukhtar Maiha, who was in the State to commission an ultra-modern veterinary hospital in Ado Ekiti and inspect ongoing projects of the Livestock Productivity and Resilience Support (LPRESS) across the state. Highlighting the importance of developing the livestock sector to the state’s economic growth, Governor Oyebanji noted that livestock development holds significant potential to boost agricultural productivity, create employment, improve livelihoods, and contribute to the state’s economic development. The Governor stressed the need for a stronger partnership between the state and federal governments to harness opportunities in the sector, particularly through strategic interventions that would strengthen livestock production and the value chain in the state. item.title: CAN disowns cleric, reaffirms neutrality ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has disowned a cleric claiming to represent the association, declaring that he is not its General Secretary and warning against attempts to use its name to mobilise support for political candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections. The association said it had neither authorised the cleric nor the group he represents to organise political activities in its name, stressing that their actions and political positions should not be mistaken for CAN’s official position. In a statement by its president, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, the association identified Archbishop Chivir Chianson as the individual in question, insisting that he had no mandate to speak or act on its behalf and that his group had no official affiliation or institutional relationship with CAN. “For the avoidance of doubt, Archbishop Chivir Chianson is not the General Secretary of CAN and has no authority or mandate to speak or act on its behalf. Furthermore, the group he represents has no official affiliation, working relationship or institutional connection with CAN,” the statement said. CAN warned that it would not allow individuals or groups without official ties to the association to appropriate its identity to advance political or personal interests. The association also reaffirmed its commitment to political neutrality ahead of the 2027 elections, insisting that it would neither endorse candidates nor mobilise support for any political party. “CAN will continue to engage national issues objectively and hold political leaders accountable, irrespective of party affiliation, without endorsing or mobilising support for any political party or candidate,” Archbishop Okoh said. The association urged Christians, members of the public and media organisations to disregard claims of official representation by the cleric and his group. It urged media organisations to verify the credentials and institutional affiliations of individuals presented as CAN representatives. CAN warned that it would take appropriate steps to protect its name, identity and institutional integrity against unauthorised representation and misrepresentation. item.title: Ebonyi Issues 30-Day Ultimatum For Occupants To Vacate Defective Building
item.description: The Ebonyi State Government, through the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning, has issued a 30-day ultimatum to occupants of a structurally defective building located at No. 10 Aguluezechukwu Street, Abakaliki, directing them to vacate the premises due to severe structural safety concerns. The order followed an on-site assessment led by the Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Richard Ugo Idike, alongside the Head of the Town Planning Department, Esther Nwite, state town planners, and the ministry’s enforcement taskforce. During the inspection, Idike expressed deep concern over visible structural defects and substandard construction, describing the building as an immediate threat to life and property. “The state government will not compromise on the safety of residents. Our ministry remains committed to ensuring that all structures across Ebonyi State strictly adhere to approved building codes and regulatory standards,” Idike stated. He explained that the 30-day window provides the property owner time to undertake necessary structural remediation to prevent a catastrophic collapse, while giving occupants sufficient lead time to secure alternative accommodation. “This notice is necessary to avert building failure and protect human lives. Occupants must make alternative arrangements before the expiration of the deadline to avoid tragic outcomes,” the Commissioner added. Idike emphasised that the ministry will step up monitoring and enforcement across the capital to detect unsafe structures, warning that non-compliant properties will face swift regulatory intervention. The exercise aligns with the urban renewal and public safety mandate of the Ebonyi State Government under Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru to maintain an orderly and secure capital city. The Ministry’s Taskforce Team urged property owners, developers, and builders across the state to strictly follow approved building plans, engage certified professionals, and use high-grade construction materials to prevent structural failures. Occupants of the affected property are expected to comply fully with the vacate order within the stipulated 30-day period. item.title: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim elected US senator
item.description: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s US Senate race over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, US networks said early Wednesday, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. “Michigan, we did it!” El-Sayed said in a speech attended by hundreds of supporters who screamed and hugged each other at his election headquarters in Detroit. “I am so proud and honored to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.” El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curve ball in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour. The Michigan medical administrator rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal health care, to win a key US Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters. El-Sayed held a nearly six-point lead on Rogers when networks called the race. “We are sick and tired of being sick and tired. And I’m so proud of all the work. It was boots on the ground. We were always out, but we were never outworked,” said party-goer entrepreneur Trunetta Roach, 75, who attended El-Sayed’s victory party in downtown Detroit wearing US flag-design diamante high-heels. “I’m feeling elated. The kids are all right. I was concerned about them. They didn’t seem very engaged, but I was wrong. They showed up.” – ‘Swear me in’ – Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans. But the straight-talking 42-year-old El-Sayed pledged to help cash-strapped voters navigate America’s fractured, for-profit health care system. “You deserve to be able to see a doctor without getting a huge bill,” he told Michiganders on the eve of the vote, vowing to upend America’s divisive multi-billion-dollar for-profit medical system. During the race, El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas. El-Sayed also vowed to get “money out of politics” and address the harsh economic woes that have voters yearning for a political newcomer to shake up the status quo. The victory made El-Sayed the first Democratic doctor in the Senate since 1969. “Everybody in politics is so trash. So to see ethical Muslims be at the forefront representing us and showing everybody what we’re actually about… it means everything,” said micro-influencer Maryam Bozai, 28. At the victory party, crowds gathered around TVs tuned to left-leaning cable news channel MS NOW, cheering jubilantly each time the Democrat’s trademark blue flashed on screen to announce another race won by the party. “Tsunami! Tsunami!” chanted Ondine Fortune, 64, a Democratic Party media planner. El-Sayed supporters rubbed shoulders with left-leaning influencers and union activists, a group that lent El-Sayed their formidable campaign infrastructure to reach Michigan’s large organized labor community. item.title: 2027: Tinubu will win second term based on achievements – Alausa
item.description: The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win re-election in 2027, saying his administration’s achievements will secure him a second term. Alausa, recently appointed Director of Education Sector Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, said opposition parties lacked a clear agenda for Nigerians. He made the remarks on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday, accusing opposition politicians of being motivated by envy and lacking the capacity to govern. “Whatever nonsense these people (opposition) are talking about is out of sheer envy. They can’t deliver, they have been tested, they have no clue of what to do for Nigerians,” Alausa said. “This president is giving Nigerians tangible benefits. Let’s be objective, that is what we have said and I am very unapologetic about this, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will win his second term squarely based on his achievements.” The minister said Tinubu had transformed different sectors of the economy and deserved another term based on his administration’s performance. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has transformed every sector of this country and he deserves to be re-elected come January 16, 2027, based on his accomplishments,” he said. Alausa urged Nigerians to disregard opposition parties, accusing them of seeking to create divisions rather than offer a viable alternative to the ruling APC. “And please, let’s not listen to the opposition parties, they don’t have any clear agenda for this country. They are just there to cause division amongst us,” he added. The minister also cited the Federal Government’s relationship with the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) as evidence of Tinubu’s achievements in the education sector. According to him, the administration has fulfilled its agreement with the union and is making progress towards ensuring that university students complete their programmes within the stipulated four-year period. Alausa said Tinubu’s commitment to preventing four-year university programmes from extending beyond their duration was being fulfilled. He also noted that ASUU had not embarked on a strike since Tinubu assumed office, presenting the development as evidence of improved relations between the government and university lecturers. item.title: Meet Keisha Lance Bottoms, first black woman elected Governor of US State
item.description: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has made history after winning Georgia’s gubernatorial election, becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US state. Bottoms, a former mayor of Atlanta, defeated Republican businessman Rick Jackson in Tuesday’s election, according to projections by US media, securing a landmark victory for Democrats in one of the country’s most closely contested political battlegrounds. The 56-year-old will also become Georgia’s first female governor, succeeding Republican Brian Kemp, who is leaving office after serving two consecutive terms. Beyond her political career in Georgia, Bottoms previously served as a senior adviser to former US President Joe Biden and director of the White House Office of Public Engagement. Her victory represents a significant milestone for Black women in American politics, who have historically played an important role in the Democratic Party but remain underrepresented in the country’s highest elected positions. Bottoms’ achievement came on the same night Stacey Plaskett was elected governor of the US Virgin Islands, becoming the first Black woman to lead a US jurisdiction. In Florida, Republican US Representative Byron Donalds also won the governorship, making him the first Black Republican elected governor in the United States. Bottoms’ victory marks a major political shift in Georgia, where Black voters have formed a central part of the Demo cratic coalition that helped transform the traditionally Republican state into a national electoral battleground. Republicans had controlled Georgia’s governorship for more than two decades before her election. Her Republican opponent, Jackson, is a billionaire businessman and founder of healthcare staffing company Jackson Healthcare. He campaigned as a political outsider, promising tax cuts, improved public safety and reduced government regulation. Bottoms’ emergence as governor comes eight years after fellow Democrat Stacey Abrams became the first Black woman nominated for governor by a major US political party. Although Abrams lost Georgia’s gubernatorial elections in 2018 and 2022, her campaigns helped build a multigenerational and multiracial coalition that increased Democratic voter participation. The mobilisation also contributed to the election of two Democratic US senators and helped deliver Georgia’s electoral votes to a Democratic presidential candidate for the first time in decades. Bottoms’ election now adds another chapter to the growing representation of Black women in American political leadership. item.title: ‘Americans want unity, not division’ – Obama reacts to Democrats’ midterm victory
item.description: Former United States President Barack Obama has reacted to the Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the midterm elections, saying Americans have called for unity and leaders capable of providing practical solutions to the country’s challenges. Obama made the remarks in a statement shared on his official X account on Wednesday, congratulating Democratic candidates who secured victories across different regions of the country. He said the election results reflected Americans’ desire for a political culture that prioritises bringing people together rather than deepening divisions. “Tonight, the American people sent a clear message — they want a politics that brings people together rather than divides them, and leaders who offer concrete solutions to the challenges they face,” he wrote. The former president attributed the party’s success to candidates who contested elections across the country, including in constituencies previously considered difficult for Democrats to win. According to him, the candidates came from diverse backgrounds and represented different political perspectives but shared a commitment to public service and the interests of their constituents. “These results were only possible because outstanding candidates stepped forward in every region of the country — including in areas once considered long shots,” Obama said. He also acknowledged the contributions of election officials and volunteers from both political parties, commending them for ensuring a smooth electoral process. “We also owe a debt of gratitude to the thousands of election officials and volunteers from both parties who helped ensure a smooth election and carried out one of the most essential functions of our democracy,” he added. Despite the Democratic victory, Obama noted that the administration would remain in office for another two years, urging party members to use their newly secured legislative influence to advance changes and limit further damage. “While this administration has another two years in office, our job now is to roll up our sleeves, make changes wherever we have the power to do so, prevent further damage, and lay the groundwork for the future,” he said. The Democrats’ midterm victory is expected to give the party greater control over the legislative process, including congressional investigations, spending negotiations and scrutiny of President Donald Trump’s administration. The outcome could also shape the final two years of Trump’s presidency, as Democrats prepare to challenge several of his policies and exercise their oversight powers in Congress. item.title: North Korea’s Kim vows to build ‘most advanced’ warships
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un vowed to possess “the most advanced and powerful warships” while touring a shipyard, state media reported Wednesday, as Pyongyang accelerates an ambitious naval expansion. Kim toured the Nampho Shipyard on Monday, where North Korea is building a new warship, the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. The nuclear-equipped country has been rapidly upgrading its navy, commissioning 5,000-tonne destroyers and testing ship-launched missiles, while Kim has pledged to arm the fleet with nuclear weapons and build larger 10,000-tonne warships. Pyongyang says the expansion is needed to counter threats from the United States and South Korea, as North Korea develops weapons designed to extend its military reach beyond its traditionally coastal navy. Kim said the “recently emerging geopolitical environment and the hostile acts of adversaries” demonstrated “the need to possess the most advanced and powerful warships”, according to KCNA. The warship under construction has a “combat system possessing operational capabilities that no other country in the world has”, Kim said, stressing the “significant military importance of this enormous concentration of combat power”. “He (Kim) said this was because we must defend our homeland, guarantee our sovereignty and deter all threats.” Kim expressed “great satisfaction” after inspecting the vessel and said it was “incomparable to the destroyer built last year”. The unprecedented operational capabilities could indicate plans to equip the new ships with “strategic cruise missiles (Hwasal series), tactical nuclear weapons, or ship-to-ship and ship-to-surface missiles”, Lim Eul-chul, professor at the Institute for Far Eastern Studies at Kyungnam University, told AFP. North Korea last year unveiled a 5,000-ton destroyer-class vessel, that experts believe can carry both ship-to-surface and ship-to-air missiles. Kim’s shipyard visit came a day after North Korea test-fired strategic cruise missiles, following a separate test of cluster bomb warheads over the weekend. Separately, Kim’s sister warned the United States on Wedendsay that her country will mount a stronger response to Washington’s “invariable hostile policy” toward Pyongyang. item.title: Democrats to challenge Trump’s policies, launch investigations after midterm election victory
item.description: Democrats are preparing a legislative offensive against US President Donald Trump after their sweeping midterm victory handed them control of both chambers of Congress and the power to challenge his policies, investigate his administration and block his nominees. Emboldened by victories deep in traditional Republican territory, the party is promising swift action on living costs and the war in Iran, while signaling that investigations of alleged abuses and corruption will be a major priority. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is in line to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress takes office in January, vowed to go after what he described as “unprecedented corruption” in the government. “Because if you have people in high office who are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends, or their donors, then they’re not focused on making life better for the American people,” he said. But Democrats will not have a free hand. Trump retains his veto, while Senate rules allow Republicans to obstruct most legislation. Here are the opportunities — and obstacles — ahead. – First 100 hours – Jeffries has promised an ambitious legislative push in the House’s first 100 hours, focused on affordability — the issue that dominated an election shaped by tariffs, high prices and the Iran war. His priorities include restoring expired Affordable Care Act health insurance subsidies, reversing nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts enacted under Trump, rolling back tariffs and pressing for an end to the conflict, which has sent fuel costs soaring. With majorities in both chambers, Democrats can bring their proposals to votes and take charge of spending negotiations. They could use federal budget deadlines to demand concessions, although confrontations over spending risk government shutdowns. – ‘Lawyer up’ – Oversight may offer an even more immediate means of challenging Trump. Robert Garcia, the Democrat expected to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee, fired off a blunt election-night message to Republicans on social media: “LAWYER UP.” Oregon Senator Ron Wyden was even more concise, posting a single word: “Subpoenas.” With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny. Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Democrats have also signaled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles. Democrats could pursue Trump’s third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so. item.title: 5 things to know about Nigerian professor Dapo Akande elected ICJ judge
item.description: Nigerian-born legal scholar Professor Dapo Akande has been elected as a judge of the International Court of Justice (ICJ), marking a significant milestone in his career and a diplomatic victory for the United Kingdom. Dapo Akande, who originally qualified as a lawyer in Nigeria, will serve a minimum nine-year term as one of the 15 judges of the United Nations’ principal judicial organ. His election comes at a time when international law is facing increasing scrutiny, with the ICJ playing a prominent role in resolving disputes between countries and addressing major international legal questions. Akande is an internationally recognised expert in public international law and has advised and represented parties in cases before international courts and tribunals, including the ICJ. Following his election, he expressed gratitude to the countries that supported his candidacy, pledging to discharge his responsibilities independently and impartially. “I am deeply honoured to be elected to the international court of justice. “I am incredibly grateful to all the states that have put their faith in me. I pledge to serve with independence and to deciding cases on the basis of a faithful and impartial application of the law. I look forward to contributing to the ICJ’s vital work in helping to resolve disputes by peaceful means, alongside the other colleagues elected today,” he said. His Nigerian legal background has remained an important part of his professional journey, which has taken him to some of the most prestigious legal and academic institutions in the world. 2. He is a professor at the University of Oxford Akande is a professor of public international law at the University of Oxford, United Kingdom. item.title: Yamal breaks Mbappe’s record as UCL’s highest-scoring teenager [See top 5]
item.description: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal has surpassed Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé to become the highest-scoring teenager in UEFA Champions League history. The 19-year-old set the new record after scoring in Barcelona’s 3-0 victory over Aston Villa on Tuesday. Yamal capitalised on a defensive error by Villa in the seventh minute at Spotify Camp Nou, curling the ball beyond goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to register his 14th Champions League goal. The goal moved him past Mbappé, who previously held the teenage scoring record with 13 goals in the competition. Although the France international has scored 72 Champions League goals overall, Yamal has now claimed the record after just 37 appearances in Europe’s premier club competition. The Spain international has also established several other milestones in the tournament, including becoming the youngest player to start a Champions League match proper. Yamal achieved that feat at the age of 16 years and 83 days when he made his full European debut against FC Porto. His latest achievement comes after an impressive showing at the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards, where he finished third behind Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane and Mbappé. The Barcelona youngster has also enjoyed a productive start to the new season, recording 13 goals and 11 assists in 15 appearances across all competitions. item.title: Soludo seeks pharmacists’ support against fake drugs
item.description: By Steve Oko Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for stronger collaboration with the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) to tackle fake drugs, improve healthcare delivery and position the state as a major pharmaceutical hub. Soludo made the call while declaring open the 99th Annual National Conference of the PSN, tagged Ijele 2026, in Awka. Speaking on the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact,” the governor described pharmacists as indispensable partners in building an efficient and sustainable healthcare system. He urged the professional body to work with his administration to enforce standards and sanitise the pharmaceutical sector, particularly by tackling counterfeit medicines and illegal operators posing as licensed pharmacies. Soludo said his administration was consolidating Anambra’s position as a pharmaceutical hub through the development of a pharmaceutical hub in Oba and a Coordinated Wholesale Centre, which he said was expected to be completed early next year. The governor also highlighted his administration’s investments in education and healthcare, saying the provision of free education from kindergarten to secondary school had reduced the state’s out-of-school children rate to 0.25 per cent, which he described as the lowest in the country. He further disclosed that the state had strengthened its primary healthcare system, provided free antenatal services to more than 250,000 beneficiaries and conducted over 950 free caesarean operations for expectant mothers. Earlier, PSN President, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, commended Soludo for his support for the pharmaceutical profession. Ibrahim described Anambra’s hosting of the conference as the fulfilment of a longstanding commitment and praised the governor’s leadership and vision. He said the conference provided an opportunity to deepen cooperation between the pharmaceutical profession and government towards improving healthcare delivery. item.title: Meet Nigeria’s Oluwatobiloba Mide-Ibrahim, the executive helping U.S. immigrant families build wealth
item.description: By Efosa Taiwo When Oluwatobiloba Mide-Ibrahim took on the challenge of helping immigrant families and businesses navigate financial decisions in the United States, the goal went beyond providing financial services. It was about helping people build stability, overcome financial barriers and make informed decisions in a new environment. Nearly five years after FinServe Pro began operations on January 1, 2022, the company’s Chief Operating Officer says its work has reached more than 4,000 individuals and businesses, with a continued focus on empowering immigrant communities. “People see the numbers, but what I see are the families behind them,” Mrs. Mide-Ibrahim said in an interview. “A mother filing for the first time with an ITIN. A small business owner who finally has clean books. A family that waited ten years to buy a home and finally got the keys. That is what these years mean to us.” Mrs. Mide-Ibrahim joined FinServe Pro as Vice President on November 20, 2021, before the firm opened, and was promoted to Chief Operating Officer on February 10, 2026. She oversees daily operations across four service lines: accounting, tax, insurance, and loans. She holds a BSc in Business Administration from Lagos State University, an MBA from the University of the People, and a Business Analytics certificate from Harvard Business School Online. The firm’s community work extends well beyond its office. FinServe Pro has sponsored or supported more than 40 community events and has spoken in schools, mosques, and churches. It has appointed brand ambassadors from among comedians, entertainers, and teachers, and has delivered free financial education through webinars, seminars, and its Wealth Spectrum series. The firm has also taken part in government initiatives, including free tax filing under the IRS Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program. The firm has received recognition. In 2024, FinServe Pro received the Innovative Company of the Year award from the Global African Diaspora Awards (GADA). In 2025, it was honoured at the NIBAD Nigeria Independence Ball and Diaspora Awards Financial Services Company for Immigrants. It also received the African Community Service Award (ACSA) Impacting Lives Award in 2025. GADA nominated the firm as Financial Services Company for Immigrants in November 2026. Asked what she had learned, Mrs. Mide-Ibrahim pointed to trust. “Many of our clients managed their finances somewhere else for ten or twenty years before they came to us,” she said. “Trust is earned slowly. We earn it by being consistent, by explaining everything, and by treating every client’s numbers as if they were our own.” Looking ahead, she described a phase of visibility and expansion. “Our first five years proved that our community is willing to learn, ready to abide, and able to pay,” she said. “The next five are about reaching the many people who still have not found the table.” Vanguard News The post Meet Nigeria’s Oluwatobiloba Mide-Ibrahim, the executive
